A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniNav and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Corresponding content can be matched despite reformatting. v1 ends with references; v3 adds Appendix A.1.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation benchmark results, component ablations, and qualitative real-robot demonstrations in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds training-data and model-size ablations with qualitative failure analysis in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The fast–slow architecture, continuous-waypoint flow-matching policy, frontier memory, and two-stage training remain unchanged. v3 clarifies parameter sharing and the subgoal-to-waypoint interface without establishing a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Training sources, navigation tasks, benchmark coverage, and real-world demonstrations are retained. Appendix A.1 uses the existing HM3D-OVON Val-Unseen setting. Newly cited GOAT-Bench is not evaluated, and the multi-floor discussion explains existing HM3D processing.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparison methods, and CityWalker remains the point-goal comparator. Removing citations from several Table 2 rows does not remove those baselines. The new model-size experiments are internal ablations.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 adds individual data-source omission controls and 3B-versus-7B comparisons with and without supplementary data. Table 1 removes the depth-input marks for Uni-NaVid and CorrectNav while retaining their scores; this revises reported settings without establishing reruns. Existing benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations, Appendix A.1 separately tests Embodied Q&A, grounding/referring, and general MLLM data, then examines the interaction between model size and additional data. It also reports object-specific failure analysis. These substantially expand the investigation of the paper's central data-versus-capability explanation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the navigation experiments. The added appendix continues reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the CityWalker results retain their numerical values. Appendix Tables 4–5 add data-omission scores of 56.5, 56.7, and 57.0, and 7B scores of 57.2 without additional data and 57.9 with it. These are supplementary results under new configurations, not improved scores for the retained main experiments.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), including waypoint encoding, the flow-matching objective, and Euler integration, are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and v3's coordinate-processing explanation does not introduce a new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim of the 'first unified architecture' with support for multiple goal modalities under one training framework and policy. This narrows the novelty claim; the main claims about navigation performance, fast–slow coordination, and general-purpose training data remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially broadens interpretation and limitations: it discusses fast-system loops and poor coverage, explains the slow system's sensor requirements, and explicitly leaves full slow-system physical deployment and latency analysis to future work. Appendix A.1 interprets model-size results through data sufficiency and identifies persistent difficult object categories and limits to the scaling study.

D1.justification: v3 specifies shared VLM parameters in Figure 1, documents local-coordinate transformation and ground-plane projection in Section 4.2, and adds sensor-modality information to Table 2. It also supplies GitHub and project-page pointers. These are additional disclosures; the stated training hardware, durations, and deployment configuration are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused frontier-navigation discussion covering GOAT, GOAT-Bench, and heuristic exploration, plus comparisons with scene-graph and semantic-map memory. References associated with BC, DAgger, RL, DAgRL, and BCRL are removed while their comparison rows remain. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites architectural explanations and experimental discussion, adds a data-processing paragraph and appendix, and updates author information. The main section sequence and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different visual template, including a colored title panel, wider text area, revised typography, and colored citations. Figure 1 gains clearer interface labels and a parameter-sharing legend; Table 2 gains observation columns; Tables 4–5 are added. Other figures are largely retained with formatting or placement changes.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.1 adds useful controls supporting the training-data argument, while the expanded implementation explanations and explicit deployment limitations improve clarity and transparency. The gains are limited by unchanged main benchmark evidence, absent uncertainty estimates for small model-size differences, and reduced citation traceability for several baselines. Overall, the improvement is useful but incremental.
